On July 14, 2026, Cambridge Day reported that the City halted demolition at 66 Kinnaird Street after determining that demolition had begun without the required permits, as documented in SeeClickFix #22254206, which remains open.

That SeeClickFix submission specifically requested that the City correct all deficiencies associated with the demolition permits for both 66 and 68 Kinnaird Street before demolition resumed, ensure compliance with hazardous-material requirements, and coordinate with the Massachusetts Department of Labor Standards (DLS) where appropriate.

The permitting and hazardous-material issues are particularly significant because DLS subsequently issued a Cease and Desist Order concerning the site. Accordingly, the unresolved question is not simply whether a City permit had been issued, but whether the deficiencies that caused work to be halted, including the matters addressed by DLS, were fully resolved before work resumed.

issue_description:
There is a message-board trailer parked right in the bike lane on JFK St at Memorial Drive, and it takes up the whole lane. There's no "Bike Lane Closed" sign, no cones, and nothing warning you to merge, so every person on a bike gets pushed out into traffic with cars, trucks, and buses. That's happening in an area with extremely high bike lane usage and a large number of students. 

I ride from North Cambridge to Lower Allston every day, and JFK near Memorial Drive was already the most dangerous part of my commute before the trailer showed up. Now it's worse.

MUTCD Part 6 says work zones have to accommodate bikes, and this does the exact opposite. It also flies in the face of the City's Vision Zero commitment. A sign meant for drivers has no reason to be sitting in the bike lane, so putting it there without so much as a warning sign isn't an oversight. It's gross negligence.
